title: True-scale system view (4/4): space cruise boost (Shift) for the 10 km legs between planets
description: SCALE DECISION (human-approved 2026-10-06), part 4. With the world rendered at true scale (TASK-82..84), planets are 10 km apart (PLANET_ANCHOR_SPACING_M). At the catalogued top speeds (scout 120 m/s after TASK-81) one leg takes ~85 s of holding W, which is too slow for the explore/mine/sell loop. Landing (20 m pads, 1 km atmosphere) and dogfights must keep today's speeds. Design: holding SHIFT in the SPACE regime engages CRUISE — the class top speed × CRUISE_SPEED_FACTOR (4) and acceleration × CRUISE_ACCEL_FACTOR (2) — but only in open space, at least CRUISE_CLEARANCE_M (1 500 m) outside every atmosphere boundary. Releasing Shift (or entering the clearance zone) lets the existing soft cap bleed the excess speed off at 5 %/tick (~4 s from cruise to normal top speed — the natural 'drop out of cruise'). Scout leg time becomes ~25 s. Movement is fully server-authoritative (the server integrates the inputs; clients never send positions), so the rule lives in the SHARED integrator and is enforced identically by the server tick, the client predictor and (never boosting) the AI.

steps.details: `src/shared/physics/flight.ts`: add `boost?: number` (0..1, default 0) to `ShipInput` and `cruiseAllowed?: boolean` (default false) to `FlightOptions`; export CRUISE_SPEED_FACTOR = 4, CRUISE_ACCEL_FACTOR = 2. In integrateShip/integrateStep, when `regime === 'space' && input.boost > 0 && options?.cruiseAllowed`, use maxVelocity × CRUISE_SPEED_FACTOR and acceleration × CRUISE_ACCEL_FACTOR — including in the TASK-81 'thrust never exceeds maxVelocity' clamp (it must use the EFFECTIVE max) — otherwise the class values. The per-tick soft cap uses the effective max too, so after release the excess decays exactly as today. New pure shared helper in `src/shared/regime.ts` (or a new small `src/shared/physics/cruise.ts`): `export const CRUISE_CLEARANCE_M = 1_500;` and `cruiseAllowedAt(pos: Vec3, planets: RegimePlanet[]): boolean` — true when the 3D distance to every planet anchor is >= its atmosphereRadius (use ATMOSPHERE_BOUNDARY_M for airless planets too, so you cannot cruise into an island) + CRUISE_CLEARANCE_M. Write these unit tests FIRST: scout boosting in deep space tops out at 480 (±1e-9, never above); boosting with cruiseAllowed false or in 'atmosphere' tops out at 120; after release at 480 the speed decays monotonically to <= 121 within 6 s; boost = 0 reproduces the committed golden fixtures EXACTLY (no fixture regeneration in this task — if they change, you broke the default path); cruiseAllowedAt false at 2 400 m from an anchor, true at 2 600 m.

`src/shared/protocol/inputs.ts`: ship mapping — `action: 'boost'` ↔ `boost: 1` (the `action` field is already a free string, schemas.ts ~line 339; no schema change). `up > 0` (VTOL, atmosphere only) still maps to 'vtol' and wins if both are set. `shipInputToPayload` / `inputToShipInput` must round-trip every channel (extend the existing round-trip test). On-foot mapping (`inputToCharacterInput`) is unaffected — 'run' stays 'run'. Server: wherever the shard tick calls `integrateShip` for PLAYER ships, pass `cruiseAllowed: cruiseAllowedAt(ship.pos, this.regimePlanets)`. AI ships keep ZERO_SHIP_INPUT-style inputs with boost 0 — do not give the AI cruise. Unit test in a shard test: a player ship sending boost in deep space exceeds 120 m/s within 5 s of thrust; the same near a planet does not.

steps.description: Client: Shift in the space scheme, predictor, HUD tag
steps.details: `src/client/input/controls.ts`: add a `boost: Key | null` to `ControlScheme` — 'Shift' in the space scheme (main.tsx already captures Shift as the key name 'Shift', see `keyOf` ~line 1411), null in atmosphere/surface — and set `boost` in `readInput`. `ClientShipPredictor` (src/client/net/prediction.ts): pass `cruiseAllowed: cruiseAllowedAt(state.pos, systemRegimePlanets(system))` into the integrateShip options it uses (extend its context with the regime planets via `setContext`), so prediction matches the server. `scaleLookDemand` (TASK-55) must leave boost untouched. Ship HUD (src/client/ui/ship-hud): show a 'CRUISE' tag next to the regime indicator while boost is held AND allowed at the predicted position; show 'CRUISE BLOCKED' (dim) while Shift is held but not allowed — players must understand why it does nothing near planets. Keep the text accessible (TASK-54 contrast/shape rules).

New `app/tests/e2e/cruise.spec.ts`: fresh player, undock, teleport to deep space { x: 0, y: 50, z: 4 000 }, hold W + Shift for 8 s → server-reported speed (entity_update tap from flight.spec.ts) > 300 and the HUD shows 'CRUISE'; release Shift, keep W for 6 s → speed <= 121. Then teleport to 2 km from planet 0's anchor ({ x: 8 000, y: 300, z: 0 }), hold W + Shift 6 s → speed <= 121 and 'CRUISE BLOCKED' visible. Screenshot `.ralph/screenshots/TASK-85-1.png` mid-cruise (TASK-83 planet proxies growing ahead if facing them). Record measured leg time (spawn-side deep space → planet 0 clearance boundary) in the LOG entry. Then `cd app && npx tsc --noEmit`, full `npm run test` (golden flight fixtures unchanged), e2e: cruise, flight, chase-camera, rogue-ai, pvp-kill, landing, keyboard-only, walk (Shift = run on foot must still work); `eslint --fix` + `prettier --write`. Commit `feat(TASK-85): ...`.

acceptanceCriteria: Holding Shift in open space (>= 1.5 km outside every atmosphere boundary) raises the ship's top speed ×4 and acceleration ×2; near planets, in atmosphere and on the surface Shift does nothing to the ship
Releasing Shift drops out of cruise smoothly via the existing 5 %/tick soft cap; the TASK-81 thrust clamp uses the effective (boosted) max
Server, client predictor and wire mapping agree (shared rule, round-trip tests); AI never cruises; golden flight fixtures are unchanged (boost defaults to 0)
HUD shows CRUISE / CRUISE BLOCKED; Shift still means run on foot
E2E `cruise.spec.ts` green with the leg time recorded; `npx tsc --noEmit` green; full `npm run test` green; touched e2e specs green; one commit
notes: Do NOT change SHIP_CLASSES numbers or PLANET_ANCHOR_SPACING_M — travel time is tuned only through CRUISE_SPEED_FACTOR / CRUISE_ACCEL_FACTOR / CRUISE_CLEARANCE_M, which a human may adjust later.
Out of scope (note as follow-ups in the LOG entry, do not build): a combat lockout (no cruise for N s after firing/being hit), cruise audio/visual streak FX, an autopilot to the nav target.
Do NOT commit the pre-existing dirty `.ralph/screenshots/*.png` mods.
